# How to train for your first marathon (26.2 miles)

Training for your first marathon is about building endurance gradually, staying healthy, and preparing your body to run 26.2 miles (42.2 km).

The biggest piece of advice: **Don't try to run fast. Train consistently, build mileage gradually, and focus on finishing.**

Most beginner marathon plans take **16–20 weeks**, although someone new to running may need several additional months to build a solid running foundation first. [www.rei.com](https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/training-for-your-first-marathon.html?msockid=0937efcd1bea62ea1c62f9601a3363bf&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.mayoclinichealthsystem.org](https://www.mayoclinichealthsystem.org/hometown-health/speaking-of-health/planning-for-your-big-run?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[health.clevelandclinic.org](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/how-to-train-for-a-marathon?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 1\. Build a foundation before starting

Before beginning a marathon-specific plan, aim to be comfortable with\:

- Running 3–4 times per week.
- Running approximately 15–25 miles per week.
- Completing a comfortable 5–8-mile run.
- Recovering without persistent pain or excessive fatigue.

If you're starting from zero, consider working toward a 5K, then a 10K, and eventually a half marathon before beginning marathon training.

You don't need to rush this process. [www.texashealth.org](https://www.texashealth.org/areyouawellbeing/Staying-Fit/Preparing-For-Your-First-Marathon-Safely?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[akronmarathon.org](https://akronmarathon.org/assets/download_files/2026_First_Time_Marathon_Guidebook.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rei.com](https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/training-for-your-first-marathon.html?msockid=0937efcd1bea62ea1c62f9601a3363bf&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 2\. Follow a 16–20-week training plan

A typical beginner program includes four or five running days per week.

Here's what a sample training week might look like\:

| Day | Workout |
|--------|--------|
| Monday | Rest |
| Tuesday | 3–5 miles easy |
| Wednesday | Strength training or cross-training |
| Thursday | 4–6 miles easy |
| Friday | Rest |
| Saturday | Long run |
| Sunday | 2–4 miles recovery |


Distances are illustrative and should be adjusted to your current fitness and training plan.

## 3\. Gradually increase your long runs


The weekly long run is one of the most important workouts.

An illustrative progression might look like this\:

| Training stage | Long run |
|--------|--------|
| Early | 5–7 miles |
| Building | 8–10 miles |
| Developing | 12–14 miles |
| Advanced preparation | 15–17 miles |
| Peak training | 18–20 miles |


You don't need to run the full marathon distance during training.

Many beginner plans build toward an 18–20-mile long run, followed by recovery and tapering. Include easier weeks periodically rather than increasing distance every week. [prod.nyrr.org](https://prod.nyrr.org/news/2025/08/08/marathon-training-faqs?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.texashealth.org](https://www.texashealth.org/areyouawellbeing/Staying-Fit/Preparing-For-Your-First-Marathon-Safely?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rei.com](https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/training-for-your-first-marathon.html?msockid=0937efcd1bea62ea1c62f9601a3363bf&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 4\. Run at the right pace

One of the biggest mistakes beginners make is running too fast.

Use these three types of running\:

- **Easy runs\:** Comfortable pace where you can hold a conversation. Most of your running should be here.
- **Long runs\:** Slow, steady efforts focused on endurance rather than speed.
- **Tempo or speed workouts\:** Shorter, harder efforts that improve fitness. Introduce these once you have a solid running base.

For your first marathon, prioritize endurance over speed. ## 5\. Incorporate strength training
![Krachttraining voor hardlopers: deze 10 oefeningen maken je sneller én sterker](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/PeeNTWZWoRtZlLTxThDmsUwLmrBLPz_6DzSYme_XgoNAg_-yR7gBT6bry7q5Ol82Q6PRE0SKFK3ICZ-1i_kkxjUrLkp_V6rSTsxWaoadDIGT7UsSkgY226AOzmOqyyCx0zBsYgIAkHPsvjt8HFMHCBl8Zkpu2nKEKeXVNL5uTllz1ZPHWD4TEPDOo0R5Vy31?purpose=fullsize)![Krachtoefeningen voor hardlopers: walking lunges](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/8N-Mce3OLH2ERXKz3sQuKf9ELlGa2gNYCInKxGomcCsZiGnHXBZaS6S3Yj1v1_VmvhIyw9zTt8hi2LFhYtzZVVsHq6Hrsx2aIZkoukAOUCGlCOo409w4FnIg12GuiWtACyrzQTaLB7VKBm8ZscVDEffFyJWQQxdOBl7p7LISuAwBAiPXXVnSCZayEFq1VZQO?purpose=fullsize)![Strength Training for Runners | Fleet Feet](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/3-YouE-DXKmhemcY3dlxmQBMIy3GYdxnR_aB5KxH-Aoz0G7JE6cMyhGJTML54oIUUDUEC5gBXYZq7Rpm-kfw1TPXrY-CZMt_RSA4MJzM3DXQJ8FPMF1Qx1TKilNfebEAHe_qb0j2jShVZ8HtVinbDeLllzbxu6rutiP8mSIs1EBLgeyqVCrpaDTyJPyN0LhF?purpose=fullsize)

Aim for two strength sessions per week, focusing on\:

- Squats
- Lunges
- Calf raises
- Glute bridges
- Planks
- Core exercises

Stronger legs, hips and core help you handle the physical demands of longer runs. [www.rei.com](https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/training-for-your-first-marathon.html?msockid=0937efcd1bea62ea1c62f9601a3363bf&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[blogs.bcm.edu](https://blogs.bcm.edu/2025/11/04/marathon-training-tips/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.mayoclinichealthsystem.org](https://www.mayoclinichealthsystem.org/hometown-health/speaking-of-health/planning-for-your-big-run?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.on.com](https://www.on.com/en-us/stories/marathon-training-schedule-for-beginners?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 6\. Practice nutrition and hydration

Don't wait until race day to figure out what works.

**During training\:**

- Eat balanced meals with sufficient carbohydrates and protein.
- Practice taking energy gels or other carbohydrates during longer runs.
- Experiment with hydration and electrolytes.
- Eat something after longer workouts to support recovery.
- Get sufficient sleep.

For longer runs, practice your race-day fueling strategy, including timing and products your stomach tolerates. [www.rei.com](https://www.rei.com/learn/expert-advice/training-for-your-first-marathon.html?msockid=0937efcd1bea62ea1c62f9601a3363bf&utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.upmc.com](https://www.upmc.com/healthbeat/sports-medicine/tips-for-first-marathon?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## 7\. Taper before race day
![International participants | London Marathon Events](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/147ldtHPP9J7VDPj7CFFpzg6AVZkAGm3XZkROzX7NVEZurW3gAm7hWADL1EuK-wKOmhm77AFoZUHMZ-kjdZzHF60f5WxZHZCXLTsnoVbbXs0-_J-z1qPnbtp9x7ZFi6uMkuv8UBwNxw1vwNhkVHrFDLQWlHKb-x1cSe0C9_KTJ1eqGJBYTprcaedZyiW82E0?purpose=fullsize)

The final 2–3 weeks before your marathon are generally about reducing training volume.

This is called tapering.

- Reduce weekly mileage.
- Keep a few short, easy runs.
- Avoid exhausting workouts.
- Prioritize sleep and nutrition.
- Don't try to squeeze in missed training.

The goal is to arrive at the starting line rested rather than exhausted. The final 2–3 weeks before your marathon are generally about reducing training volume.

This is called tapering.

- Reduce weekly mileage.
- Keep a few short, easy runs.
- Avoid exhausting workouts.
- Prioritize sleep and nutrition.
- Don't try to squeeze in missed training.

The goal is to arrive at the starting line rested rather than exhausted.
